Media & Communications, B.A.
The major in Media and Communications provides students with a broad-based education emphasizing theoretical, historical
and experiential learning in an interdisciplinary context. This major prepares students for careers and advanced study in media
studies, journalism, communications, public relations, and media production.
The B.A. in Media & Communications is grounded in the economic, political, social and intellectual history of the U.S. A wide
variety of courses offers theoretical and practical instruction in theory, journalism, broadcast (radio, TV) and new media
(podcasting and multimedia/multi-platform digital storytelling). Students will develop strong writing, news reporting, media
production, and critical thinking skills to help them assess, and participate in, the complex dynamics of media in contemporary
society.
Students also gain practical experience through internships on campus at student media hubs (radio, TV , digital news, and
cross-platform media). Proximity to the New York Metropolitan area provides exciting off-campus internship opportunities in a
variety of fields such as digital and broadcast news, television, radio/podcasting, sport media, digital journalism, public
relations, strategic communications, social media and more.
Students in other majors who are interested in media can minor in Media & Communications or Media Design. The department
also offers micro-credentials in AI & Society, Fundamentals of Non-Fiction Video Production and/or Television News
Production, Advanced TV/Video Production, Multimedia Journalism, and PR and Strategic Communications.
Evening Students
A limited selection of Media and Communications courses are available in the evening. Completion of a major in Media and
Communications typically requires daytime course attendance.
Transfer Students
A Media and Communications major can be completed in a two year period with appropriate planning. With an advisor’s
approval, a maximum of five courses will be accepted in transfer toward the 12 courses required for the major. Transfer
students should note that the “Knowledge of American Society” course as well as AS 2802 - Multimedia Storytelling and AS
3800 - Writing for Media are prerequisites for enrollment in 5000-level American Studies courses, as well as for a number of
other courses in the major. It is essential that these requirements be fulfilled in a transfer student’s first year at Old Westbury if
the expectation of completing the program in two years is to be met. These courses must be taken prior to the senior year.

Combined B.A. in Media & Communications / M.A. in Liberal Studies
- SUNY Old Westbury
The combined B.A. in Media & Communications/M.A. in Liberal Studies program allows qualified undergraduate students to
accelerate their progress toward a master’s degree. This can save time and cut overall tuition costs. Applicants will major in
Media & Communications at the undergraduate level. They will complete the requirements for that B.A. degree while
beginning a portion of the graduate M.A. in Liberal Studies program in their senior year. For more information, visit the MALS
webpage: https://www.oldwestbury.edu/programs-courses/liberal-studies-ma.

8. Portfolio Recommended
All Media and Communications majors should assemble a portfolio for recognition of academic work and for employ‐
ment. The Portfolio should contain samples of work done in courses and the Internship in Media. The portfolio should
contain examples of written work, both published and submitted as class assignments, and selected graphics, radio pro‐
grams and videos.

Liberal Education Curriculum
To learn more about Old Westbury’s Liberal Education Curriculum requirements, see the LEC web page: https://www.old‐
westbury.edu/division/office-academic-affairs/liberal-education-core.
Program Policies:
1. All Media and Communications majors should see an adviser at least once a semester.
2. Only one grade of D+, D or D- will be accepted toward the major. Students must request this inclusion from the chair
of American Studies.
3. A minimum GPA of 2.0 must be achieved in the major.
4. Only two 1000 or 2000 level courses will be counted towards the major beyond AS 2802 and the “Knowledge of
American Society” courses AS 2252, AS 2262, AS 2263, AS 2300, AS 2640.
5. Only one course from the Visual Arts Department will be counted toward the major.
6. In order to qualify for independent study, students must have at least sophomore standing and a B (3.0) average. Only
four credits of independent study will be counted toward the major.
7. Only four credits of internship can be applied toward the major. Students can take up to twelve credits which will be
counted as elective credit toward graduation, but only four will be applied toward the major. Students must see an
adviser to plan their internship.
